  says.
- Leave the `##` headings, the `<!-- key: ... -->` comments and the `###`
  field names alone. They are how the text finds its way home.
- Keep any `%s` and `%d` exactly as they are. The game fills them in with a

- Blank lines inside a passage are kept. Leading and trailing ones are not.
- Speaker names are part of the line ("Elder: Good morning."). The dialogue
  box splits them off itself, so keep the `Name: ` prefix.

## The Stair Shut

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_04_the_stair_shut.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_04_the_stair_shut.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** warden · **Turn-in:** aldric

**Follows:** `quest_main_03_the_black_knight`

### title

The Stair Shut

### summary

The Oathbreaker has stood aside and the altar is open. No warden has ever seen what lies under it, but forty-one champions went down before and the seal held every time, so somebody below knows their business.

### offer_line

The knight has stood aside and the altar is open. Only champions can go down.

What I can tell you is that the Order has sent forty-one before you and the seal has held forty-one times, so somebody down there knows their business. Find them.

### accept_option

I'll go down.

### refuse_option

Give me the night.

### accepted_line

Take the offerings with you and do not set them down for anything. I will be at the ruins when you come up.

### refused_line

Then take the night. The seal has held this long and it will hold till morning.

### reoffer_line

The altar is still open and the stair is still waiting. Have you decided?

### progress_line

Still up here? The stair is behind the altar. Mind the first step; it is a long one.

### continue_option

I'm going down.

### abandon_option

Not today.

### abandoned_line

No shame in it. Every champion I have sent down stood where you are standing and needed a moment. Come back when you have had yours.

### complete_line

Another one. Put the scroll away, lad, I'm no wild thing. Aldric of the Order, champion of the ninth watch, and I heard that door open from three halls off. Come and sit by the fire. 

There are more of us down here than you are expecting, and we have been keeping things ready a long while.

### done_line

They keep the halls below. Whoever they are, they have kept them well. Do as they tell you.

---

## The Archivist's Table

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_04_to_the_archivist.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_04_to_the_archivist.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** aldric · **Turn-in:** archivist

**Follows:** `quest_main_04_the_stair_shut`

### title

The Archivist's Table

### summary

Forty-one champions came down this stair before, and every one of them is written up in the Archivist's book. Aldric will not let anyone go deeper without hearing what is in it.

### offer_line

Before you go a step further into these halls, you are going to sit down with the book. The Archivist keeps it at her table, over by the lamps. Everything anyone has learned down here is in her hand, and most of it was paid for. Go and let her tell you what you are walking into.

### accept_option

I'll hear it.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Across the hall, under the lamps. She will have heard the door; she always does.

### refused_line

Sit with it a while, then. The book will keep.

### reoffer_line

Ready to hear what is in the book?

### progress_line

The Archivist. Her table is across the hall, under the lamps.

### complete_line

The Archivist: Aldric sent you to be frightened properly. Sit. You will want to know what you are walking into, and I am the one who writes it down.

### done_line

Everything is in the book. Come and read it whenever you like.

---

## The Record

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_05_the_record.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_05_the_record.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** archivist

**Follows:** `quest_main_04_to_the_archivist`

**Recommended level:** 18 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Record

### summary

The Archivist keeps the book of every champion who came down the stair and everything they learned about the king before the wood took them. One roll is still out in the northwest hall with the woman who was writing it.

### offer_line

You will want to know what you are walking into, and I am the one who writes it down. Every champion who came down that stair is in my book, and so is everything they learned about him before the wood had them. 

One roll is still out in the northwest hall with the woman who was writing it. She got as far as the pillars. Bring her roll home and I will read you the whole of it, from the bargain forward.

### accept_option

I'll bring it back.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

The squires between you and it were champions once, same as her. They have forgotten what they were told to do and they are still doing it. Be quick, and be kind.

### refused_line

Then it stays out there, and so does she. Come back when you would rather know than not.

### reoffer_line

The roll is still in the northwest hall. Would you fetch it now?

### progress_line

Northwest hall, past the crypts. She is sitting down, and the roll is under her hand.

### continue_option

Still looking.

### abandon_option

I'd rather not.

### abandoned_line

As you like. I have waited four hundred years to finish that entry; I can wait a little longer.

### complete_line

The Archivist: Thank you. Now sit, because this is the oldest thing in the book and I have had a long while to get the wording right. 

The king loved something and lost it, and grief took his reason, and when a man with a crown loses his reason he does not weep, he acts. 

He went to the god of the dead and asked for what no living man may ask, and he was answered. 

That is the whole of it. He does not live and he does not die; he sleeps, and the sleep wears thin, and every few decades somebody has to press him back into it.

His knights went with him because they were sworn and the oath dragged them along behind him. 

They are being punished for his crime. 

So are we. So is the wood. Go and see the Gravewright down the east passage when you are ready; he will show you what these halls cost.

### done_line

The Gravewright is down the east passage. He has been waiting on a pair of hands.

### caution_line

A word. Those squires were champions, and this ground has not made them gentler. Come back when your lead is nearer level %d and it will be a shorter afternoon.

## The Gravewright's Rows

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_05_to_the_gravewright.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_05_to_the_gravewright.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** archivist · **Turn-in:** gravewright

**Follows:** `quest_main_05_the_record`

### title

The Gravewright's Rows

### summary

Nothing goes up that road unpaid for. The Gravewright works the rows where the halls' dead are laid, and what he lifts out of them is what the next champion carries.

### offer_line

Now go and see the Gravewright, and go quietly; he is out among the rows. He lifts the seal-iron off the ones the halls take, so it can go home with somebody who is still walking. You will be carrying some of it before long, so you may as well know whose it was.

### accept_option

I'll go to him.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Out past the crypts, where the ground is opened. Do not tread on the names.

### refused_line

When you are ready. They are not in a hurry.

### reoffer_line

Ready to go out to the rows?

### progress_line

The Gravewright is out among the rows, past the crypts.

### complete_line

Mind where you tread. They are all champions, every one of these, and you are standing on the ninth watch.

### done_line

Tread softly and take what the iron gives you.

---

## The Bell-Hall

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_06_to_the_bellkeeper.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_06_to_the_bellkeeper.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** gravewright · **Turn-in:** bellkeeper

**Follows:** `quest_main_06_what_the_dead_carry`

### title

The Bell-Hall

### summary

Somebody has been ringing the bells by hand since before the town had a name, and she is losing both of her posts at once. The Gravewright will not let the player go past the bell-hall without stopping in it.

### offer_line

The Bellkeeper wants you next, and she is not a woman who asks twice. Through the far arch and down, where the rope hangs. Whatever she tells you in there, believe the unpleasant half of it.

### accept_option

Through the arch, then.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Far arch, then down. You will hear the rope before you see her.

### refused_line

She has waited on champions before. She will wait on you.

### reoffer_line

Ready to go down to the bell-hall?

### progress_line

The bell-hall. Far arch and down, where the rope hangs.

### complete_line

You are the one from upstairs. Good.

### done_line

When the bells ring, somebody is pulling. Remember that.

---

## What the Dead Carry

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_06_what_the_dead_carry.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_06_what_the_dead_carry.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** gravewright

**Follows:** `quest_main_05_to_the_gravewright`

**Recommended level:** 21 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

What the Dead Carry

### summary

The Gravewright digs for the champions these halls take and lifts the seal-iron off them so the sigil can go home even when they cannot. Two lie where he cannot reach, with Mirelashes sitting over both.

### offer_line

Mind where you tread. They are all champions, every one of these. I dig for the ones the halls take, and I lift the seal-iron off them, because the iron can go home even when they can't.

Two are out where I cannot reach, one under the southwest flood and one at the old camp, and there are Mirelashes sitting over both. 

Bring their sigils in. They should not be left lying in his halls.

### accept_option

I'll bring them in.

### refuse_option

Not now.

### accepted_line

The Gravewright: Water and earth put a Mirelash down. Don't let one get its mouth on you; they hold.

### refused_line

The Gravewright: They have lain there a long time. They will lie a while more.

### reoffer_line

The Gravewright: Those two are still out there. Changed your mind?

### progress_line

The Gravewright: Southwest flood and the old camp. Any luck?

### continue_option

Still at it.

### abandon_option

I can't face it.

### abandoned_line

The Gravewright: I'll not press you. It is not pleasant work and it was never yours to do.

### complete_line

The Gravewright: Both of them. Good. Half of this goes in the ground with their names on it and half goes to the Sealwright, and the Sealwright cuts it into scrolls, and the scrolls go to you. No coin, don't offer. That is how this place works: the last one leaves the next one better off than they were. Forty-one times we have done it, and every champion who walks up that road carries something one of us paid for. Take them. The Bellkeeper wants you next. She is in the bell-hall and she is shouting about it.

### done_line

The Gravewright: Bell-hall, north end. She has not stopped shouting.

### caution_line

The Gravewright: Those Mirelashes are heavier than anything you met upstairs. Nearer level %d, if you want my advice, and you should, because I bury the ones who didn't take it.

## The Inside of the Door

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_07_the_inside_of_the_door.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_07_the_inside_of_the_door.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** bellkeeper

**Follows:** `quest_main_06_to_the_bellkeeper`

**Recommended level:** 24 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Inside of the Door

### summary

The Bellkeeper has two posts: the rope that warns the Reach when the sleep thins, and the inside of the altar door, which the halls have held for four hundred years. The bell-hall is overrun and she cannot keep both.

### offer_line

You are the one from upstairs. Good, then you can be useful. 

I have two posts and I am losing both. One is the rope: I ring when the sleep thins, and that is the only reason your Elder ever knows anything. 

The other is that door above us, which I hold from this side, because things come up these halls whenever he stirs and not one of them has ever reached your town. They are in my bell-hall now. 

Clear them out and I can ring and hold at once again.

### accept_option

I'll clear it.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

The Bellkeeper: The gazers first. They hang high and they slow you, and the Bulwarks are trouble enough without being slow.

### refused_line

The Bellkeeper: Then I hold it with one hand and ring with the other, as I have before. Go on.

### reoffer_line

The Bellkeeper: The bell-hall is still full of them. Well?

### progress_line

The Bellkeeper: North end, under the rope. Are they down?

### continue_option

Still working.

### abandon_option

It's not my post.

### abandoned_line

The Bellkeeper: Suit yourself. It is not your post. It was never supposed to be anyone's.

### complete_line

The Bellkeeper: Quiet. Listen to that. First quiet in a month. Go and find the Nurse at the camp before you go any further. She has been watching you come and go.

### done_line

The Bellkeeper: The Nurse is at the camp in the great hall. Go and be looked at.

### caution_line

The Bellkeeper: I would not send you in at this size. Those Bulwarks do not move and do not care. Level %d, and bring something that mends.

---

## The Nurse's Bench

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_07_to_the_nurse.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_07_to_the_nurse.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** bellkeeper · **Turn-in:** nurse

**Follows:** `quest_main_07_the_inside_of_the_door`

### title

The Nurse's Bench

### summary

Nobody goes up the last road on a party held together with luck and good manners. The Nurse keeps a bench at the camp and has been watching the player cross the hall once too often.

### offer_line

The Bellkeeper: Go and find the Nurse at the camp before you go any further, and do not argue with her, because I have tried it. She has been watching you come and go.

### accept_option

I'll see her.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

The Bellkeeper: Back up in the hall, at the bench by the fire. She will have a word ready.

### refused_line

The Bellkeeper: She will still be there, and she will have had longer to think about it.

### reoffer_line

The Bellkeeper: Ready to be looked over?

### progress_line

The Bellkeeper: The Nurse. At the bench by the fire, up in the hall.

### complete_line

The Nurse: Stop there. I have watched you cross this hall four times now and your Oathbound are held together with luck and good manners.

### done_line

The Nurse: Come to the bench whenever something needs mending. That is what it is for.

## The Road to the Bench

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_08_a_champions_kit.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_08_a_champions_kit.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** nurse

**Follows:** `quest_main_07_to_the_nurse`

**Recommended level:** 26 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Road to the Bench

### summary

The Nurse keeps the only bench in these halls, and nobody can be carried to it. Hexcallers hang over the east hall and two Ironhorns stand in the crypt road, and she will not clear a champion for the stair while the wounded cannot reach her.

### offer_line

The Nurse: Stop there. I have watched you cross this hall four times now and your Oathbound are held together with luck and good manners, and I will get to that in a moment. 

First you can do something for me, because I am the only bench in these halls and lately nobody can reach it. Three Hexcallers have come up into the east hall. 

They put a hand on a man's head and he forgets which way the fire is. Past that, on the crypt road, two Ironhorns are standing square in the way. 

Open that road for me. I am tired of being told to wait while somebody bleeds two halls off.

### accept_option

I'll open the road.

### refuse_option

I'm fine as I am.

### accepted_line

The Nurse: Hexcallers first, and do not give one a second turn at you. The Ironhorns will stand still until you are close, and then they move all at once.

### refused_line

The Nurse: Then go up the road half-ready, like the last forty did. I will keep a bed clear.

### reoffer_line

The Nurse: The east hall and the crypt road. Have you come to your senses?

### progress_line

The Nurse: Hexcallers in the east hall, Ironhorns on the crypt road. It is not a difficult list.

### continue_option

I'm getting to it.

### abandon_option

I don't need fussing.

### abandoned_line

The Nurse: Fine. It is your road. I have never once enjoyed being right about this.

### complete_line

The Nurse: The road is open. Good. Now sit down and let me look at your Oathbound, because that was always the half you were dreading.

Every champion who goes up that road goes up carrying what the last one paid for. That is the whole of this place. That is why we stayed. 

Go and find Aldric at the stair down. He has been standing in the mouth of it since the bells rang and he will not say why.

### done_line

The Nurse: Aldric is at the stair down. Go gently with him about it.

### caution_line

The Nurse: I have buried people who went at Ironhorns light. Level %d, and bring something that mends, or you will be on my bench instead of beside it.

---

## Back to the Stair

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_08_to_aldric.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_08_to_aldric.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** nurse · **Turn-in:** aldric

**Follows:** `quest_main_08_a_champions_kit`

### title

Back to the Stair

### summary

Read, resupplied and put back together, there is nothing left in the camp to be handed. Aldric has been standing in the mouth of the stair since the bells rang, and he is the one who opens it.

### offer_line

The Nurse: That is everything this camp can put in your hands. Go back to Aldric, at the stair down. He has been standing in the mouth of it since the bells rang and he has been waiting for somebody to be ready. Today that is you, and I have run out of reasons to keep you here.

### accept_option

Back to the stair.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

The Nurse: He is where he always is. He does not sit either.

### refused_line

The Nurse: Rest first, then. It is the one order I can give you.

### reoffer_line

The Nurse: Ready to go back to Aldric?

### progress_line

The Nurse: Aldric. At the stair down, where he always is.

### complete_line

Aldric: So she has finished with you, and you came back up the hall on your own feet. Good. Then it is time you heard what is below this one, and who is standing in it.

### done_line

Aldric: The stair is behind me. It will be there when you are.

---

## The Kingsworn

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_09_the_kingsworn.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_09_the_kingsworn.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** aldric

**Follows:** `quest_main_08_to_aldric`

**Recommended level:** 27 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Kingsworn

### summary

One of the king's own knights stands in the stair down to the wood and has stood in it for four hundred years. He was sworn to a man who went to the god of the dead, and the oath took him along whether he willed it or not.

### offer_line

Aldric: There it is. That black throat in the wall is the way down to his wood, and the thing standing in it is one of his own knights. Kingsworn. 

He has stood in that gap four hundred years and he says the same four words to everyone who comes near it. 

Not while I hold this door. 

He is not cruel and he is not mad. He was sworn to a man who went to the god of the dead, and the oath took him along whether he willed it or not, same as the one you beat at the altar. He does not want to be there, but this one He will kill you.

### accept_option

I can take him.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

Aldric: He fights like a man holding a doorway, because he is. He will not chase you and he will not tire. Wear him down and keep something back for the end; he saves the worst of it for when you think it is over.

### refused_line

Aldric: Then he keeps the door another day. He has kept it longer.

### reoffer_line

Aldric: The Kingsworn is still in the stair. Are you ready for him?

### progress_line

Aldric: He is where he has always been. Take your time. I have.

### continue_option

I'm going back in.

### abandon_option

I can't beat him.

### abandoned_line

Aldric: I am the last man alive who is going to think less of you for it.

### complete_line

Aldric: Good job besting him.

I carried the rite to that doorway thirty years ago and I stood in front of him and I knew, the way you know a thing in your chest, that I did not have it in me. 

So I turned round and I came back to this fire, and the day I set the rite down was the day the stair stopped knowing my name. 

That is my business and not yours. Go on down. The wood is his own ground and it is nothing like these halls. 

Find the champion who keeps the stair at the bottom; she has been there longer than I have been down here, and she will tell you the road.

### done_line

Aldric: Down the stair and look to your left. She sits against a dead tree and she will not get up. Let her tell it her way.

### caution_line

Aldric: I will not talk you out of it. I will say this: he is stronger than the knight at the altar, and the knight at the altar was the kind one. Level %d at the least. Train in the halls; he is not going anywhere.
